two_d_renderer.decision: promote native SVG visuals plus a semantic HTML hit-target layer
why: Native SVG supports one fixed viewBox, crisp code-native isometric geometry, palette CSS variables, LOD groups, and reusable skill symbols through symbol/use without a dependency.
Real HTML buttons retain consistent keyboard, focus, touch-target, and screen-reader semantics while sharing the same worldToScreen camera transform.
The current Canvas2D/DOM hybrid validates this separation, but Canvas2D would require a new custom asset command system for reusable geometry, palette slots, LOD visibility, and hit testing.
A third-party 2D scene graph is unjustified because the accepted scope requires fixed authored geometry, pan/zoom, selection, and overlays rather than physics or a generalized editor.
render_contract: One SVG owns illustrative geography and buildings and is aria-hidden; one adjacent landmark navigation layer owns real buttons and accessible labels.
Each accepted skill asset is defined once as an SVG symbol keyed by the canonical asset ID; every city-local instance uses that symbol plus employer palette variables and a fixed transform.
Each project has one unique symbol and one fixed instance. LOD child groups may become visible, but the instance ID, root transform, footprint, orientation, and silhouette never change.
No complete generated scene is shipped as layout truth. Accepted SVG paths or deterministic geometry data are registered assets.

The initial renderer must add no runtime dependency and no perpetual animation loop. Ambient motion, if later approved, uses a separate optional Canvas2D layer and stops for reduced motion/background tabs.

rejected_alternatives.option: Canvas2D as the primary authored-world renderer
rejected_alternatives.reason: Useful for ambient effects but weak for inspectable reusable asset identity, SVG asset ingestion, palette slots, LOD grouping, and maintainable hit targets.
Would turn vector geometry and reuse into a large set of brittle CSS boxes and pseudo-elements.

rejected_alternatives.option: Add Pixi, Konva, Phaser, Three, or Babylon for the 2D world
rejected_alternatives.reason: No demonstrated 2D requirement justifies a scene-graph or WebGL dependency.

fixed_coordinate_semantic_zoom.status: promote contract shape; numeric geography waits for the accepted CW-001 coordinate sheet
fixed_coordinate_semantic_zoom.world_space: WorldRegistry owns one immutable WorldBounds and every city, project, and skill position in world units. Responsive layout fits that same space; it never recalculates entity coordinates.
fixed_coordinate_semantic_zoom.camera_type: type WorldCamera = { center: { x: number; y: number }; zoom: number }
fixed_coordinate_semantic_zoom.projection: fitScale = min(viewportWidth / worldWidth, viewportHeight / worldHeight); screen = viewportCenter + (worldPoint - camera.center) * fitScale * camera.zoom
state_contract: WorldFocus is a discriminated union of world, employerId, or projectId; project ownership is resolved from the registry, not parsed from copy.
Selecting an employer or project changes only camera target and selection emphasis. It does not replace the scene or recompute positions.
Project activation completes the project-focus camera transition and then opens ProjectDrawer. drawerOpen is separate state and must not alter camera, coordinates, or SVG instance identity.
Reduced motion jumps to the same target without interpolation. Escape closes the drawer and restores the project button; a separate back action returns project to employer and employer to world.
URL state preserves the existing project deep-link ID where available; an employer parameter is explicit. Invalid IDs fall back to world without manufacturing content.
invalidations: If the accepted art sheet uses a different aspect ratio or coordinate extent, change WorldBounds once before composition; do not alter the camera/state contract.

If SVG path count or paint time is measured as a bottleneck after the full accepted asset library exists, rasterize only immutable decorative sublayers or move ambient effects to Canvas2D; keep semantic instances and hit targets unchanged.

reuse_without_rewording: EvidenceTrace title, shortTitle, statement, summary, proofLabel, evidenceClass, outcomes, limitations, and artifacts.
EvidenceRecord sequence, source, evidenceClass, title, detail, nodeIds, and weight for project flows.
GraphNode IDs and labels as candidate skill vocabulary, subject to the explicit visible-skill decision.
projectSkillRelationships supportKind/evidenceIds as audit input for evidence-backed links, not as physical placement.
traceById and recordsForTrace behavior, or equivalent neutral exports, for factual drawer lookup.
new_or_normalized: EmployerRegistry: explicit employerId, city asset ID, palette ID, fixed city instance, focus target, public label, and evidence availability.
ProjectRegistry: explicit projectId, employerId, project asset ID, fixed instance position/orientation, evidenceTraceId or null, and content status. Never infer employer from period or title.
SkillAssetRegistry: canonical visible skill ID, geometry asset/version, footprint, palette slots, LOD groups, and mapping to a GraphNode ID when one exists.
SkillInstanceRegistry: one fixed employer/skill instance with one palette and position; enforce uniqueness of employerId + skillId.

ProjectSkillLink: projectId -> skillInstanceId, based only on the Director-approved visible-skill matrix. The current projectId/nodeId derivation can seed review but cannot create buildings automatically.
Asset status: candidate, accepted, or retired. The renderer rejects candidate assets in production composition unless the current ticket explicitly runs the placeholder tracer.
Evidence boundary: world entities remain illustrative; evidenceTraceId is the only route from a project building to factual copy. Projects with null evidenceTraceId show no invented inspector.
data_reuse_and_normalization.migration_boundary: Keep evidence-data.ts unchanged during CW-003 and isolate the old-feature import in features/career-world/model/evidence-adapter.ts. After the 2D world is stable, CW-006 may move factual data/inspector code to a neutral portfolio-evidence feature with compatibility re-exports; do not combine that mechanical move with renderer work.

later_3d_boundary.decision: defer engine selection and all 3D source/dependencies until CW-007 is green
later_3d_boundary.why_not_now: No accepted scene complexity, interaction model, asset format, or measured bundle budget exists, so choosing Three.js, Babylon.js, or another engine now would be dependency-first architecture.
required_interface: The 2D project drawer owns factual content. The 3D scene receives only illustrative asset IDs/palettes and emits navigation events; it cannot author evidence claims.
The 3D module is dynamically imported only after explicit activation. It must not be imported by app/page.tsx, the initial CareerWorld module, or the registry.
No WebGL, load failure, context loss, or reduced motion falls back to the unchanged 2D project-focus state with a concise explanation.
The 3D camera cannot rotate or reinterpret canonical city/project/skill identity unless a later accepted contract explicitly supersedes the fixed authored view.
risks: Initial JS and parse cost if an engine leaks into the root chunk.
GPU memory, shader compilation, context loss, mobile thermal throttling, and background-tab work.
Keyboard/camera traps, pointer-lock surprises, motion sickness, missing text alternatives, and inaccessible canvas-only controls.
Duplicate asset identity if 3D models diverge from accepted 2D registry IDs, footprints, silhouettes, or employer palette slots.
Hydration/SSR failures if WebGL globals are touched before the client-only lazy boundary.
promotion_measurements: Initial route build manifest contains zero 3D engine modules.
Post-activation chunk size and load time are recorded on desktop and a mobile-class throttle before an engine is accepted.
Frame time, memory/context-loss recovery, reduced motion, keyboard exit, and 2D fallback are captured as QA artifacts.
